evals.prompt: The gaku-api pod is in CrashLoopBackOff. I have no idea what's wrong. Can you find out what's causing it?
evals.expected_output: A structured Problem Source Report identifying the exact cause of the pod crash — specific log line, file/config/image that is broken, and a confirmation command
expectations: The report identifies the specific layer where the problem originates (k8s infra, Docker image, .NET startup, config/secret, etc.)
The agent runs kubectl describe or kubectl logs --previous (not just kubectl get pods) to gather evidence
The root cause section names a specific file, config key, image name, or code location — not just 'the pod is crashing'
The report includes a 'How to confirm' command the user can run
The agent does not assume the layer upfront — it gathers signals first and concludes from evidence

evals.prompt: The db-migrate job is failing every time it runs. I added a new migration yesterday for waypoints. The Web app won't start properly either.
evals.expected_output: A structured Problem Source Report tracing the migration failure to its root cause — specific migration file, SQL error, or schema conflict
expectations: The agent reads the migrator pod logs (not just job status) to find the exact error message
The root cause names a specific migration file in src/Gaku.Infrastructure/Migrations/ or a schema conflict
If there is a SQL error (e.g. 'relation does not exist', 'already exists'), the agent explains what caused it in terms of the migration code
The agent checks whether the issue is also the reason the Web app won't start (traces the dependency)
The report includes a 'How to confirm' command

evals.prompt: GET /api/trails/nearby keeps returning 500. The map on the home page won't load — it just shows a spinner. I haven't changed anything in the API recently.
evals.expected_output: A structured Problem Source Report tracing the 500 to its root cause — specific exception in pod logs, traced to the file and line in src/ responsible
expectations: The agent reads gaku-api pod logs to find the exception and stack trace for the failing request
The agent traces the exception into source code — finds the relevant file and line in src/
The root cause section identifies the specific method and file causing the 500, not just 'there's an exception in the API'
The agent checks whether the problem is in the repository layer (PostGIS query, ST_DWithin) or application layer (service, DTO mapping)
The report distinguishes between the symptom (spinner / 500) and the actual root cause (the specific code or config that is broken)
